cards.explanation: The answer is that the LORD will forgive the city. He says, “If you can find a single person, anyone who acts justly, anyone who seeks the truth, then I will forgive the city.” Notice who gets the benefit: the whole city, not just the one person who gets found. One person like that on the streets, and Jerusalem is forgiven. That's a door left wide open.

The answer is False. The text says, “Although they say, ‘As surely as the LORD lives,’ they are swearing falsely.” The words are in their mouths, and the oath is false anyway. A stamp can press a perfect word into dough, friends, but that doesn't mean the cookie is any good.

The answer is repent. Verse 3 says, “They have made their faces harder than stone and refused to repent.” The LORD struck them and they felt no pain. He finished them off, and they refused to accept discipline. That's a lot of hard chances turned down.

The answer is the powerful. The speaker says, “I will go to the powerful and speak to them. Surely they know the way of the LORD, the justice of their God.” He'd just called the poor fools who don't know the way of the LORD, so he figures the people at the top must do better. He's about to find out.

The answer is False. The speaker expected better from the powerful, but verse 5 says, “But they too, with one accord, had broken the yoke and torn off the chains.” So the powerful aren't keeping the way of the LORD. It's the same story at the top as it was lower down.

The answer is that their rebellious acts are many. Verse 6 says why a lion, a wolf and a leopard come against them: “For their rebellious acts are many, and their unfaithful deeds are numerous.” That's a heavy picture, friends, and I think this part of the passage is a hard one. The text gives the reason plainly, and it's what the people have done.

The answer is gods that are not gods. Verse 7 says, “Your children have forsaken Me and sworn by gods that are not gods.” Back in verse 2 they were swearing falsely by the LORD's name. Now the LORD says they've sworn by gods that aren't gods.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “I satisfied their needs, yet they committed adultery and assembled at the houses of prostitutes.” He took care of them, and they still went away from Him. This one is heavy, and I think it hurts to read.

The answer is that the LORD asks, “Should I not punish them for these things?” Then He asks again, “Should I not avenge Myself on such a nation as this?” He's just listed what they've done, and now He asks about it. This part is heavy, friends, so take a breath.

The answer is that He says not to finish them off. The LORD says, “Go up through her vineyards and ravage them, but do not finish them off.” There's a limit set right inside the order. The damage comes with a line it must not cross.

The answer is that they do not belong to the LORD, and it's the only reason He gives. He says, “Strip off her branches, for they do not belong to the LORD.” Not too wild, not out of fruit. If a cookie box with a stranger's name on the lid showed up in my bakery, I wouldn't ask how pretty the cookies look. I'd ask whose box it is.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have been utterly unfaithful to Me…” Both houses are named, and the word is “utterly.” That's a heavy thing to say about both of them.

The answer is that they say He will not do anything. Verse 12 says they lied about the LORD and said, “He will not do anything; harm will not come to us; we will not see sword or famine.” The text calls it a lie, and it reports it as their words.

The answer is False. The people say, “The prophets are but wind, for the word is not in them.” That's the opposite of saying the prophets carry the LORD's word. They also say, “So let their own predictions befall them.”

The answer is a fire. The LORD says, “…I will make My words a fire in your mouth and this people the wood it consumes.” The people called the prophets wind, and He answers with fire. Wind and fire, friends. Those are the words, right there.

The answer is that the people won't know its language. The LORD calls it “…a nation whose language you do not know and whose speech you do not understand.” Imagine a nation showing up, and you can't make out a single word they say. It's one more way the LORD says they will be strangers to His people.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “With the sword they will destroy the fortified cities in which you trust.” The cities don't hold off this nation. Notice that the people trusted in them. It's a heavy verse, and I think it's hard to read.

The answers are gods and foreigners. The LORD says, “Just as you have forsaken Me and served foreign gods in your land…” and then, “…so will you serve foreigners in a land that is not your own.” This is His answer to the people's question about what offense they committed. They served foreign gods in their own land, and now they will serve foreigners in a land that isn't theirs. The two halves of the sentence line up.
